mathematical_reason: Cornell MATH 304 §4.1.3 defines a rational Cauchy sequence by arbitrarily tight pairs of entries in a tail. This quantifies over all positive rational tolerances and all pairs of sufficiently late indices. It does not assume an existing limit in Q or R, nor is it the weaker requirement that successive differences tend to zero.

Sloughter's real-number construction defines equivalence of rational Cauchy sequences by eventual rational epsilon-closeness at matching indices. Reflexivity and symmetry follow immediately, while transitivity uses the triangle inequality with epsilon/2. The definition must not refer to equality of real-valued limits, since the reals are still being constructed.
